validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE confirmed independently: WhiteWater Midstream took FID on the Pelican Pipeline Oct 30-31, 2024 (prnewswire.com FID release, already cited) and announced a capacity upsize July 30, 2025 (prnewswire.com capacity-expansion release, already cited) -- both read to exhaustion. Independent analyst coverage: East Daley Analytics, 'WhiteWater's Pelican Project Tackles Louisiana Capacity Shortage' (2024-11-13, eastdaley.com/daley-note/whitewaters-pelican-project-tackles-louisiana-capacity-shortage), an original piece (not a wire reprint) naming the same FID, 170 mi, 36-inch (pre-upsize), Williams LA-to-Gillis routing, and 1H2027 in-service target, and placing the project in the competitive Haynesville-egress landscape alongside LEG/LEAP/Gulf Run. Third origin: EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook tracks 'Pelican Pipeline' (WhiteWater Midstream, LA, Authority=LA DNR -- i.e. an intrastate line, FERC silence is expected) across 7 releases 2025-01 through 2026-08, independently confirming existence, scope and the status/spec history below. Also cross-checked the routes-repo geometry (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7831.geojson): 3 features starting near 32.21N/-93.49W (consistent with the Williams, LA / Bienville-Webster Parish area named as the origin) and ending near 30.44N/-93.20W (consistent with the Gillis Hub/Ragley, LA area named as the terminus); combined digitized length is ~153.5 mi (main line alone ~133.3 mi) against a stated 170 mi -- plausibly a straighter digitization of an as-built/planned corridor rather than a wrong pipeline; not flagged as a route concern since no source disputes the termini. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas both correct -- every source describes a large-diameter (36in at FID, upsized to 42in), high-capacity, ~170-mile line moving Haynesville-basin gas from a production area (Williams, LA) to a demand hub (Gillis, near Ragley, LA) that serves Gulf Coast/LNG markets; that is a transmission line, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 44-row roster -- Pelican is a distinct WhiteWater greenfield project, not a relabeling of Louisiana Energy Gateway (P5115, Williams/Williams-affiliated), LEAP (P6843, DT Midstream), Delhi Connector (P2523), Gillis Access Extension (P7807) / Transco Gillis West (P7808), NGPL TX-LA Expansion (P7832), Delta Express (P2737), or Magnolia (P2559) -- East Daley explicitly discusses Pelican as a NEW entrant competing with LEG/LEAP/Gulf Run for the same egress market, not as one of them. CAVEAT (attribution): the FID release states WhiteWater 'has partnered with FIC, Stonepeak and Trace Capital Management on the Pelican Pipeline,' but no source found (FID release, capacity release, East Daley, EIA) discloses FIC/Stonepeak/Trace equity percentages -- current sheet value (Owner1=WhiteWater Midstream 100%) is the only sourced figure and stands, but may not reflect the eventual/actual cap structure if the financial partners hold direct equity rather than debt/project financing. LEAD FOR ORCHESTRATOR (not a roster PID, so not filed as a cross_row_lead): EIA's Aug2026 release adds a new, separate project 'Pelican Thrasher Lateral' (WhiteWater Midstream, 65 mi, 42in, LA, Announced 2026-08, in-service 2029) -- a greenfield lateral off Pelican extending to Commonwealth LNG in Cameron Parish, announced ~2026-05-28 per multiple 2026 trade press (Pipeline & Gas Journal, Oil & Gas Journal, Natural Gas Intelligence, BIC Magazine, Inspenet, via Google News headlines). This has no GEM ProjectID yet and looks like a Discovery candidate for a future pass, not part of P7831 itself.

The sheet's recorded Capacity (2000.00 MMcf/d) matches neither the pipeline's original FID-stage design (1.75 Bcf/d = 1750 MMcf/d, per the Oct 2024 FID release and East Daley) nor its current, post-upsize design (2.5 Bcf/d = 2500 MMcf/d). The July 30, 2025 WhiteWater release -- already the sheet's own cited [ref] for this cell -- states verbatim: 'WhiteWater today announced the upsize of the Pelican Pipeline to a 42-inch from a 36-inch diameter pipeline. The new scope will increase the pipeline's capacity to approximately 2.5 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) from 1.75 Bcf/d.' That is why the existing_ref_check on this cell could not find '2000.00'/'2000'/'2,000' on the cited page -- the page says 2500, not 2000. Independently corroborated by the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, which shows 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' = 1750 for the 2025-01/04/07 releases and 2500 from the 2025-10 release onward (all consistent with the 42-inch diameter, which the sheet already records correctly). Diameter (42 in) is correctly recorded and already matches the upsized design; Capacity is the one figure that is stale/wrong at 2000.
